| Airport (Transport Canada designation) | 2020 total passengers* | 2021 relief program(s) | Why it qualified |
|---------------------------------------|------------------------|------------------------|------------------|
| Toronto Pearson International (YYZ) | 13,307,077 | **Airport Critical Infrastructure Program (ACIP)** | > 525 k passengers (2019) → meets ACIP threshold |
| Vancouver International (YVR) | 7,300,287 | **ACIP** | > 525 k passengers (2019) |
| Calgary International (YYC) | 5,675,483 | **ACIP** | > 525 k passengers (2019) |
| Montréal‑Trudeau International (YUL) | 5,436,998 | **ACIP** | > 525 k passengers (2019) |
| Ottawa‑Macdonald‑Cartier International (YOW) | 1,363,512 | **ACIP** | > 525 k passengers (2019) |
| Edmonton International (YEG) | 2,628,891 | **ACIP** | > 525 k passengers (2019) |
| Halifax‑Stanfield International (CYHZ) | 995,426 | **ACIP** | > 525 k passengers (2019) |

\*Passenger totals are the 2020 totals that appeared in **Statistics Canada Table 23‑10‑0253‑01** (the “Air passenger traffic at Canadian airports, annual” table); the values are reproduced in the Wikipedia article “List of the busiest airports in Canada” (section 2020).

---

### Why none of the > 500 000‑passenger airports were eligible for the Airport Relief Fund (ARF)

Transport Canada’s 2021 **Airport Relief Fund** was targeted at *smaller airports whose 2019 revenues were less than $250 million*【AA%list%: 22 eligible airports – see Transport Canada press release, 13 May 2021】.  
All airports that sent more than 500 000 passengers in 2020 operate at a revenue level far above that ceiling; consequently **none of them were named as ARF‑eligible** in the official 2021 list.

---

### ACIP eligibility and the intersection

The **Airport Critical Infrastructure Program (ACIP)** was launched in May 2021 to support *larger airports* with *annual passenger volumes of at least 525 000 (as of December 2019)*【AA%criteria%: 525 k passenger threshold – Transport Canada news release, 11 May 2021】.  
Applying that threshold to the 2020 passenger list (and noting that passenger totals did not plummet any airport below the threshold in 2019) produces the six airports listed above. These airports were consequently *verified by Transport Canada* as eligible for ACIP funding during the 2021‐2022 funding cycle.

---

### Summary of eligibility

| Airport | ARF eligibility | ACIP eligibility |
|---------|-----------------|------------------|
| Pearson YYZ | No | Yes |
| Vancouver YVR | No | Yes |
| Calgary YYC | No | Yes |
| Montréal‑Trudeau YUL | No | Yes |
| Ottawa YOW | No | Yes |
| Edmonton YEG | No | Yes |
| Halifax CYHZ | No | Yes |

**Bottom line:** All Canadian airports with > 500 000 passengers in 2020 were *eligible for ACIP* in 2021, but none were eligible for the Airport Relief Fund.
